back: The resources used to produce goods and services: land, natural resources, capital and businesses.
Resources passed down between generations; to be used productively, conserved and shared.
Government action to redistribute land ownership or use, usually from a few large owners to many people.
Increasing the share of businesses and resources owned by local (indigenous) citizens.
Giving disadvantaged people land, capital, skills, finance and markets so they can take part in the economy.
Indigenisation: ownership to local citizens. Nationalisation: ownership to the state.
Community and employee share ownership schemes, reserved sectors, loans and training for local entrepreneurs, value addition.
Foreign investors may invest less, so less capital, technology and employment; local buyers may lack finance.
Skills (extension services), finance, inputs, irrigation and markets for the produce.
